record.title: TauIndianBankBench reports that outcome-only scoring misses procedural failures in banking agents
record.summary: A paper introduces a 1,000-task synthetic Indian retail-banking benchmark for tool-using conversational agents. It scores both final database state and whether required calls—including read-only policy checks—occurred, while rejecting unrequested writes. In author-run evaluations of six models, final-state-only scoring raised pass rates by 6.5–12.0 percentage points over the paired action-plus-state criterion. The results are reported by the authors and have not been independently reproduced; simulator error, real customer behavior, non-English performance and deployment reliability remain unestablished.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The released benchmark contains 1,000 synthetic Indian retail-banking tasks and evaluates both final records and required tool calls, including policy-mandated reads; unrequested writes fail the action check.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In author-run evaluations of six models, scoring final records alone increased pass rates by 6.5–12.0 percentage points relative to the combined action-plus-final-state criterion.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that a separate scorer reimplementation matched the action-plus-state verdict on all 600 sessions and all 705 paired calls; this audit is described within the same paper and is not an external reproduction.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish real-bank customer failure rates, suitability for deployment, performance in Indian languages, or generality to other regulated service domains.

evidence_gaps.description: The 6.5–12.0-point gap and model scores are author-reported; this activation did not independently run the code or re-score the released corpus.
The authors state that error in the LLM customer simulator was not measured; all customer data are synthetic and the benchmark is English-only.
Benchmark pass rates do not establish real-world banking performance, deployment reliability or suitability.

brief.importance_rationale: If the paper-reported gap generalizes, outcome-only agent benchmarks can overstate procedural reliability in regulated service tasks, changing evaluation design. Its current scope is one synthetic, English-language Indian retail-banking benchmark and does not establish real-world prevalence.
limitations: All benchmark scores are author-reported and have not been independently reproduced here.
The benchmark uses a simulated bank and synthetic customer records; task frequencies do not estimate real customer traffic.
The customer simulator affects results and its error rate was not measured.
Version 1.0.0 is English-only; no non-English or real-bank deployment results are reported.
A pass is benchmark-specific and does not establish deployment suitability.
brief.summary: A paper introduces a 1,000-task synthetic Indian retail-banking benchmark for tool-using conversational agents. It scores both final database state and whether required calls—including read-only policy checks—occurred, while rejecting unrequested writes. In author-run evaluations of six models, final-state-only scoring raised pass rates by 6.5–12.0 percentage points over the paired action-plus-state criterion. The results are reported by the authors and have not been independently reproduced; simulator error, real customer behavior, non-English performance and deployment reliability remain unestablished.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report 6.5–12.0 percentage points more passes under final-state-only scoring across six evaluated models; an appendix reports an author-run independent scorer reimplementation matching 600 sessions. These results were not independently reproduced here.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper and released dataset describe 1,000 synthetic Indian retail-banking tasks, paired final-state/action scoring, four task categories and separate train/test subsets. The repository and dataset artifacts are publicly linked.
technical.mechanism: The benchmark compares a final-state check against an action check that requires each gold-chain call, including policy-mandated read-only calls, and rejects unrequested writes. A task passes only when both checks pass.
technical.regime: Version 1.0.0 synthetic, English-language Indian retail-banking tasks in the tau-squared-bench harness; 1,000-task base split, one deterministic attempt per task, six Gemma 4/Qwen3.8-27B model configurations and MiniMax-M2.7 simulated customer.
technical.reproducibility: The authors link source code and a 1,000-row dataset, but this activation only inspected their repository and dataset pages and did not run or independently re-score them. The authors report simulator, synthetic-data and language limitations.
technical.strongest_baseline: The benchmark’s own paired final-state-only check on the same recorded model sessions; this isolates scoring-rule differences in the reported results but does not provide an external benchmark or real-world baseline.

brief.title: TauIndianBankBench reports that outcome-only scoring misses procedural failures in banking agents
brief.why_it_matters: The benchmark demonstrates a plausible measurement failure in outcome-only agent evaluation: an assistant can leave the right records while skipping policy-required checks or making an unrequested change. If the reported gap persists under independent audit, regulated-domain evaluations may need to score process and outcome together. This is one synthetic, English-language retail-banking environment, not evidence of real-bank failure rates.
